article_title: Structural Relationships between Environmental Factors, Psychological Health, and Academic Performance in Medical Students Engaged in Online Learning during the COVID-19 Pandemic.
citation: Taleb Ola K., Sarimah Abdullah, Siti-Azrin Ab Hamid, Baharuddin Kamarul Aryffin, Abusafia Ali H. (2023). Structural Relationships between Environmental Factors, Psychological Health, and Academic Performance in Medical Students Engaged in Online Learning during the COVID-19 Pandemic. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph20021494
title: Questionnaire battery: LNT scale, technology scale, and GHQ-12 with verified GPA
description: The study used a three-part online self-administered questionnaire: a 9-item LNT scale covering "lighting, noise, and temperature", a 6-item technology scale measuring adequacy of technology for online classes, and the 12-item GHQ-12 for psychological distress, plus a 9-item proforma for sociodemographics and GPA. GPA was verified with the academic office. In this sample the measurement models showed good fit (e.g., LNT: CFI = 0.99, TLI = 0.98, SRMR = 0.03, RMSEA = 0.03).
requirements: Items were answered on five-point Likert scales, and all questions were compulsory; GPA was verified against academic office records
constraints: The technology scale's upper 90% CI of robust RMSEA was 0.16 in this sample; the study excluded students with a history of underlying psychological issues
target_learners: undergraduate medical students in online learning
target_learning_goals: measuring environmental conditions, psychological health, and academic performance in online learning contexts
examples: Administered via Google Form to 207 second- and third-year medical students at USM, completed in 20–30 minutes
key_sources: Taleb Ola K., Sarimah Abdullah, Siti-Azrin Ab Hamid, Baharuddin Kamarul Aryffin, Abusafia Ali H. (2023). Structural Relationships between Environmental Factors, Psychological Health, and Academic Performance in Medical Students Engaged in Online Learning during the COVID-19 Pandemic. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph20021494

article_title: Demonstrating Dynamic Stability in Paul Traps: Exploring Rotating Saddles with Liquid Nitrogen Droplets
citation: Laurel Barnett, Aidan Carey, Robert Hart, Daniel Davis, Anna Klales, and Louis Deslauriers. (2025). Demonstrating Dynamic Stability in Paul Traps: Exploring Rotating Saddles with Liquid Nitrogen Droplets. https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04035
title: LN2 rotating saddle demonstration apparatus with 3D-printed saddles, stepper motor, and function-generator control
description: The demonstration consists of a 3D-printed saddle (PETG, coated with Smooth-On XTC-3D) mounted via a custom adapter on a stepper motor controlled by a microstep driver receiving a frequency signal from a function generator, with rotation speed monitored via an oscilloscope. Two saddles were used: "a nearly symmetric saddle with β = 1.06, and an asymmetric saddle with β = 2.67", both with height h0 = 2.5 cm and radius r0 = 9 cm. The appendix provides fabrication details, assembly instructions, a materials cost table, and a Python script for generating saddle geometry.
requirements: A DC power supply providing at least 14.5V for the motor driver
condensation must be removed (warming with a hair dryer) between trials to maintain the Leidenfrost effect
constraints: Print times ranged from 33 to 52 hours per saddle; dark filament colors are recommended for visibility
target_learners: undergraduate physics students in lectures and laboratories
target_learning_goals: exploring rotating saddle potentials and the Leidenfrost effect
examples: LN2 is dispensed using an 8-ounce styrofoam cup with a small hole punched near the lower rim
key_sources: Laurel Barnett, Aidan Carey, Robert Hart, Daniel Davis, Anna Klales, and Louis Deslauriers. (2025). Demonstrating Dynamic Stability in Paul Traps: Exploring Rotating Saddles with Liquid Nitrogen Droplets. https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04035
